title: Chip Startup Velaura AI Hits $1 Billion Valuation With $110 Million Raise
excerpt: The Santa Clara-based company's Titan Core platform targets AI data center power costs, backed by Samsung, Premji Invest, and Seligman Ventures.
body:
• Velaura AI raised $110 million in a Series A round, valuing the chip design startup at over $1 billion
  • Seligman Ventures led the round, with participation from Capricorn Investment Group, Samsung Catalyst Fund, StepStone Group, and Maverick Silicon
  • The startup's Titan Core platform promises up to 2x lower power consumption for AI accelerators at the silicon level
  • Velaura is already engaged with three of the four largest cloud computing providers globally

Chip design startup Velaura AI said on Tuesday it has raised $110 million in a Series A funding round that values the company at more than $1 billion. The investment backs Velaura's technology for reducing power consumption and operating costs at AI data centers — a problem that has become central to the economics of scaling artificial intelligence.

Who's Backing the Bet

Seligman Ventures led the round, with new investor Capricorn Investment Group joining alongside existing backers Samsung Catalyst Fund, StepStone Group, and Maverick Silicon. Previous investors in the company include Premji Invest, Qualcomm Ventures, Mayfield, and MARA Holdings.

The funds will be used to accelerate development and deployment of Velaura's AI products and to hire engineers and customer-facing staff, the company said.

What Velaura Actually Builds

Velaura AI develops low-power chips and software technologies for data centers and physical AI applications, including robotics and autonomous systems. Its flagship product is Titan Core, a proprietary chip design platform announced earlier this year that targets the single largest power consumer inside an AI accelerator: matrix multiplication.

The technology uses low-voltage design techniques proven across tens of millions of production ASICs at the 3nm process node. Independent analysts have noted the significance of a production track record at that scale.

"The next era of AI will be defined not only by better models, but also by fundamentally better compute economics."

— Rajiv Khemani, Co-founder and CEO, Velaura AI

Khemani told Reuters the startup is engaged with three of the four largest cloud computing providers, though he declined to name them. The company charges an upfront fee for its technology plus a royalty tied to the power savings customers achieve — a model similar to Arm's per-chip licensing before it started manufacturing its own chips.

Why Power Is the AI Bottleneck

The funding arrives as AI data center power consumption has become one of the industry's most pressing constraints. AI-focused data centers grew power consumption 50% in 2025, according to the International Energy Agency. U.S. grid interconnection queues have swelled to more than 2,600 gigawatts of pending projects, with average wait times of four to five years. Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta have all signed nuclear power purchase agreements to address the gap.

SemiAnalysis estimates that half of data centers will operate behind-the-meter power by 2027, making chip-level efficiency gains increasingly valuable. Velaura's pitch — reducing the energy needed to generate AI tokens at the silicon level — addresses this from the bottom of the hardware stack rather than through infrastructure workarounds.

Indian-Origin Leadership in the AI Chip Race

CEO Rajiv Khemani, who co-founded the company in 2022, is based in Santa Clara, California. The startup's backing from Premji Invest — the investment arm of Wipro founder Azim Premji — adds to a pattern of Indian capital flowing into frontier semiconductor startups. Velaura joins a growing roster of Indian-origin-led companies competing for a share of the AI hardware market that has been dominated by Nvidia, AMD, and a handful of hyperscaler custom chip programs.
